text: This is where the last four lessons come together. Real AI API responses are nested — dicts inside lists inside dicts — and this lesson is about navigating that without it turning into a mess.
Here's a simplified but realistic shape modeled on how chat completion APIs actually respond: a model name, a list of choices, each with a nested message, and a usage dictionary with token counts.
You chain lookups — a key, then a list index, then another key. Read it right to left in your head: the response's choices, the first one, its message, the content.

Real responses sometimes omit fields. Chaining raw brackets crashes the instant one link is missing. Chain .get() calls instead, each with a sensible default, so a missing field falls back gracefully.
json.loads turns JSON text into a dict; json.dumps does the reverse — a Python dict back into JSON text, exactly what you send TO most AI APIs when you make a request.

That's the full toolkit: lists, dicts, sets, tuples, and navigating them nested. Last lesson of this chapter: file I/O — reading and writing files, including the JSON files you'll use to save and load data.
